name: Scalar casts and type checks
desc: Covers CASTBOOL, CASTNUM, CASTSTR, BOOL, NUM, and STR. Casts accept current-node or explicit value operands and enforce their specified conversions without host truthiness, loose numeric parsing, or object coercion. CASTNUM requires a whole JSON number token without surrounding whitespace; valid numeric text outside the supported host range (including nonzero underflow to zero) is UNSUPPORTED_GRAFT. BOOL/NUM/STR cover type checks, NUM inclusive/null bounds, and STR interface edges; regex algorithms and capture combinations remain in the sequence/regex suites. Fractional CASTSTR spellings are checked by round trip rather than fixed cross-platform formatting. Native Date and non-JSON number extensions require implementation-specific tests.

tests.name: CASTNUM range and fatal host limits
tests.desc: Valid tokens may exceed the implementation numeric range. Implementations that can represent these values succeed; otherwise UNSUPPORTED_GRAFT must propagate through match probes, including alternatives and negation. Malformed tokens remain INVALID_TARGET regardless of an overflowing-looking prefix. The same rule applies to nonzero values too small for the host to retain; zero mantissas with extreme exponents are still zero.

tests.name: CASTSTR permitted scalar conversions
tests.desc: Strings pass through verbatim and booleans use lowercase spellings. Integers use decimal digits without exponent notation, including large integers that host default stringification writes exponentially.
